lemma_statement: theorem isWeierstrassModel_unique (W : WeierstrassCurve R) [W.IsElliptic] {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)} {x₀ : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of R)} {x₀' : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X'} (hs : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f) (hs' : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f') (h : IsWeierstrassModel W X f x₀) (h' : IsWeierstrassModel W X' f' x₀') : ∃ e : X ≅ X', e.hom ≫ f' = f ∧ x₀ ≫ e.hom = x₀'
b2_reason: IsWeierstrassModel's points clause is a BARE pointed Equiv (cardinality only, DEF-7 form). Over R = ℚ take E, E' ℚ-isogenous non-isomorphic elliptic curves of positive rank (2-isogeny pair y²=x³−36x / y²=x³+144x, n=6 congruent). A ℚ-isogeny φ and its dual give |E(K)| ≤ deg·|E'(K)| and conversely for every ℚ-algebra field K; both sets are infinite (rank ≥ 1 is isogeny-invariant), so the cardinals agree for EVERY K and a pointed bijection exists. Hence X' := projModel E' satisfies IsWeierstrassModel (E-data) with smoothness, but the concluded pointed iso projModel E ≅ projModel E' over Spec ℚ would make E ≅ E' as elliptic curves (pointed iso + rigidity) — contradiction. KM 2.2.5 (full text now mined, printed pp. 68-69) is uniqueness of ADAPTED COORDINATES x,y for a FIXED (E/S, ω) — up to x ↦ x+a, y ↦ y+ax+b — not reconstruction of the scheme from field-point counts; the ticket statement is strictly stronger than the source and false. FIX OPTIONS for owner: (1) strengthen points to a K-NATURAL family of bijections (functor of points on ℚ-algebra fields; kills the cardinality slack — isogeny bijections are not natural), or (2) define the model property as ∃ pointed iso to projModel W (uniqueness becomes trivial, content moves to a characterization theorem), or (3) restate T-A4 in KM's actual form: uniqueness of the Weierstrass presentation of a FIXED pointed smooth proper curve, i.e. two Weierstrass data W₁ W₂ with pointed-isomorphic projModels are related by VariableChange (needs BB-RR).
counterexample: R = ℚ; W = Weierstrass data of E : y² = x³ − 36x (rank 1); X' = projModel of E' : y² = x³ + 144x (2-isogenous, E' ≇ E — distinct minimal models); both satisfy the hypotheses, conclusion forces E ≅ E'.

lemma_statement: theorem representable_iff (P : ModuliProblem R) : P.Representable ↔ P.RelativelyRepresentable ∧ P.Rigid
b2_reason: Statement (= Loeffler Thm 3.7.4 verbatim) is unsupported by either source's proof: KM's SCHOLIE (4.7.0) carries the hypothesis 'relatively representable AND AFFINE over (Ell)', which KM's proof uses three times — book p.112 (M(P,delta) affine over affine M(delta) => absolutely affine), p.113 ('Because M(P,delta) is affine, the quotient M(P,delta)/G exists'), p.114 (alpha_univ descends 'because P is relatively affine', SGA I VIII 7.8). A free finite-group quotient of a general scheme is only an algebraic space (Hironaka), and Loeffler's own quotient input (Prop 3.6.1) is stated only for QUASIPROJECTIVE X, so his sketch tacitly assumes what 3.7.4 omits. AMENDED (owner-approved 2026-07-08, option (a)): affineness added to the <= direction only, via the new hypothesis `hP : P.AffineOverEll` (KM's phrase, verbatim in the docstring). The => direction is unaffected: `rigid_of_representable` (T-E5a) is now PROVEN axiom-clean, and relative representability follows from hP. The unrestricted form is recorded as a documented non-goal in the docstring (citing KM Appendix A.4.1.2/A.4.1.3, Gabber's counterexample) and is NOT deleted.

lemma_statement: theorem gammaHNaive_relativelyRepresentable (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (H : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod N))) (hinv : IsUnit (N : R)) : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).RelativelyRepresentable ∧ ∀ X : EllObj R, ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ X.base), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧ ∀ {T} (g : T ⟶ X.base), Nonempty ({ h : T ⟶ Z // h ≫ f = g } ≃ (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).obj (Opposite.op (X.pullbackAlong g)))
b2_reason: FALSE for every H ≠ ⊥. `gammaHNaiveProblem R N H` is defined as *global* H-orbits of naive full-level-N structures, `P_H(E/S) := {H-orbits of Isom((Z/N)^2, E[N]) over S}`. This presheaf is NOT a Zariski (or fppf) sheaf, hence not relatively representable: over `T = X.base ⊔ X.base` (codiagonal g : T → X.base, gᵢ = 𝟙), the diagonal glue [(L,L)] and the twisted glue [(L, γ·L)] (γ ≠ 1 in H, glSmul the GL₂-action) have equal restriction to each summand ([L]=[L] and [L]=[γ·L] as H-orbits, since γ·L ∈ H·L) yet are distinct global sections when the H-action is free — a descent/separatedness failure. (A counting variant over étale covers kills the étale conjunct too.) SOURCES CONCUR it is a transcription slip: Loeffler Fact 3.8.1 pins P_H(E/k̄) as H-orbits only on ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED k̄ (geometric points), never as a naive presheaf on all S; his §3.6 notes the naive orbit map is 'neither injective nor surjective'; KM DEFINES P_H as the quotient moduli problem `[Γ(N)]/H` of Chapter 7 §7.1 (verbatim below), NOT as naive orbits. KM 7.1.2 (print p.187, pdf 198): 𝒫' = 𝒫/G iff (Q1) G operates trivially on 𝒫', and (Q2) for every representable δ étale over (Ell/R), 𝕸(δ,𝒫)/G exists and maps isomorphically to 𝕸(δ,𝒫') [equivalently (𝒫_{E/S})/G ≅ (𝒫'_{E/S})]. KM THEOREM 7.1.3(1),(2),(4): for 𝒫 relatively representable and affine over (Ell/R) with G finite acting, 𝒫/G exists as a relatively representable moduli problem affine over (Ell/R); if G operates freely, 𝒫 is an étale G-torsor over 𝒫/G; 𝒫 → 𝒫/G is finite. FIX (owner-delegated, B2 EVENT #2): repoint T-H4/T-H6 at the KM-7.1.2 quotient problem `P_H = [Γ(N)]/H` (corrected statements STAGED in Moduli/GammaHRepresentability.lean: gammaH_relativelyRepresentable, gammaHNaive_toQuotient, gammaH_representable_of_rigid, with the H=⊥ salvage gammaHNaive_relativelyRepresentable_bot PROVEN). The falsity is LOCKED into the library by gammaHNaiveProblem_not_relativelyRepresentable (the codiagonal counterexample, sorry-free in its own proof; residual sorryAx via gated FullLevelPt/glSmul helpers, follow-up). The naive statement is NOT deleted from GammaH.lean (theorem_statement_protected); it stands as the documented non-goal.
counterexample: H ≠ ⊥ (pick γ ∈ H, γ ≠ 1); T = X.base ⊔ X.base with codiagonal g; sections [(L,L)] and [(L, glSmul γ L)] of P_H over T restrict equally on each summand (H-orbit equality) but differ globally when the H-action on Isom is free — so P_H is not a sheaf, hence not relatively representable. Formalized: gammaHNaiveProblem_not_relativelyRepresentable.

lemma_statement: theorem gammaHNaive_representable_of_rigid (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (H : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod N))) (hinv : IsUnit (N : R)) (hrig : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Rigid) : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Representable ∧ ∀ X : EllObj R, Nonempty ((gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).RepresentableBy X) → (Smooth X.structMap ∧ IsAffineHom X.structMap)
b2_reason: Inherits T-H4's defect: T-H6 concludes representability of the same naive `gammaHNaiveProblem R N H`, which for H ≠ ⊥ is not even relatively representable (T-H4 above), so 'representable of rigid' is vacuous/false at the naive object. It also mis-cites its route: 'via representable_iff (T-E5) + T-H4' presupposes the (now-refuted) T-H4. FIX: repoint at the KM-7.1.2 quotient problem — corrected statement STAGED as gammaH_representable_of_rigid (GammaHRepresentability.lean:1205), which applies the amended KM-4.7.0 engine (representable_iff with AffineOverEll, T-E5) to P_H = [Γ(N)]/H: KM COROLLARY 4.7.2's own proof (rigidity 2.7.2 + rel-rep 3.7.1 + the 4.7 engine), with P_H rel-rep by FINITE (hence affine) étale morphisms giving AffineOverEll (KM 7.1.3(2),(4)). Gated on the KM 4.7 ⇐ engine (exists_ellipticCurveGeom_quotient, CHARTER-FP4 — geometric core + [a5] algebra now axiom-clean, a5 geometric stitch remaining). Naive statement not deleted (documented non-goal).
counterexample: Same as T-H4: for H ≠ ⊥ the naive gammaHNaiveProblem is not relatively representable, so no rigid naive P_H is representable at that object; the representability holds for the KM-7.1.2 quotient problem instead.

lemma_statement: noncomputable def geomFibrePointAddEquiv : E.Point (geomPoint B k) ≃+ (W.baseChange k).toAffine.Point (hypotheses hE, hπ; field map_add' sorried as the [T-B6'] pin)
b2_reason: map_add' is FALSE as stated: the hypotheses (hE, hπ) do not pin E.zero to projModelZero W. An AddEquiv forces 0 ↦ 0, and the underlying (proven) bijection sends exactly the MODEL zero to 0 (projModelPointsEquiv_zero) — so for any record whose abstract zero is not the model zero (a zero-shifted record still satisfies hE/hπ, which never mention zero), map_add' cannot hold. Discovered by NEW-CASCADE's [T-B6'] gate audit (v10.123-CASCADE), flagged for coordinator visibility instead of silently fixed — correct protocol. FIX (owner-delegated approval, B2 EVENT #3, coordinator v10.127): add hz : E.zero ≫ eqToHom hE = projModelZero W (or equivalent zero-pinning) to the hypotheses. Audit verified every current consumer can supply it (tateUniversal_geom / fibreCurve carry the zero identification). EXECUTION: NEW-CASCADE in the [T-B6'] fill session, same commit as the map_add' proof, quoting this entry; NEW-Y1 (IFACE holder) informed via inbox; statement change is additive-hypothesis-only, consumer-compatible.
counterexample: Zero-shift: transport a valid record's group structure along translation by a nonzero section — hE and hπ persist (neither mentions the zero section), but the shifted record's zero is not the model zero, so the equivalence would have to send a non-model-zero point to 0, contradicting projModelPointsEquiv_zero + the AddEquiv law 0 ↦ 0.

lemma_statement: theorem gammaHNaive_representable_of_rigid (N)(H)(hinv)(hrig : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Rigid) : (gammaHNaiveProblem R N H).Representable ∧ ∀ X, Nonempty (RepresentableBy X) → Smooth ∧ IsAffineHom
b2_reason: Rigid→Representable is asserted for the H-ORBIT-PRESHEAF, but representable presheaves are fppf sheaves and the orbit presheaf fails the fppf sheaf axiom at rigid H. Take H = unipotent upper-triangular (rigid for N ≥ 4: preimage torsion-free — trace ≡ 2 mod N forces no elliptic elements, -1 excluded for N ≥ 3). Twisted complement: E/ℚ with rational P of order N generating E(ℚ)[N], and Galois acting on any complement lift Q by σQ = Q + b_σ·P with nontrivial cocycle b (cyclic twist class; classical existence). Over the cyclic cover L the pair (P,Q) is an honest presheaf section; its two pullbacks to L⊗L agree as H-orbits (cocycle condition), but no section over ℚ exists (a ℚ-orbit-representative would need a RATIONAL Q). Sheaf gluing fails ⟹ not representable ⟹ the implication is false as stated. In-tree corroboration: [GHC3] (GammaHRep:3601+) records the orbit-presheaf/quotient comparison is bijective only over k̄ and NOT an isomorphism of problems for H ≠ ⊥.
counterexample: H = {(1,*;0,1)} ≤ GL₂(ℤ/N), N ≥ 4; E/ℚ with E(ℚ)[N] = ⟨P⟩ ≅ ℤ/N and complement twisted by a nontrivial cyclic cocycle; cover Spec L → Spec ℚ. Fix options: (a) RECOMMENDED restate at qpd.prob (sheaf quotient — the true statement is the existing gammaH_representable interface, proven modulo the engine); (b) add fppf-sheafiness of the orbit presheaf as a hypothesis; (c) weaken to geometric points per GHC3.
